summary: GCD and LCM of a list are built two numbers at a time: keep a running value and combine it with each next number. The LCM uses `lcm(a, b) = a × b / gcd(a, b)`.

blocks.title: Import gcd
blocks.text: `math.gcd` gives the greatest common divisor of two numbers.

blocks.title: Read the numbers
blocks.text: N, then N positive integers on one line.

blocks.title: Start with the first number
blocks.text: The GCD and LCM of a single number are that number, so both start at `nums[0]`. If N = 1 the loop doesn't run and both are printed as is.

blocks.title: Fold in each next number
blocks.text: `gcd(g, x)` shrinks the common divisor; `l * x // gcd(l, x)` grows the common multiple. `//` keeps it an `int` (`/` would make a float and can lose digits on big numbers).

blocks.title: Print two lines
blocks.text: Exact format: `GCD: 6` and `LCM: 72` on separate lines.

complexity: Time O(N log M) with N ≤ 100 — instant.
pitfalls: Using `/` instead of `//` → a float like `72.0`.
Starting the LCM at 0 — every product would be 0.
